our_argument_summary: WIN-002 (verdict Self-Contradicted) argues the dome relabels a globe-formula residual as aetheric damping and cannot internally reconcile its three claimed heights. Verified against git HEAD (data/wins.json:002): (a) the 10.59 Hz raw-theoretical is Schumann 1952 globe formula f=(c/2pi a)sqrt2, not a dome derivation (data/wins.json:002 detail_evidence); (b) the dome quarter-wave floor at H0=8,537 km is c/(4*8,537km)=8.78 Hz, requiring only ~11% damping vs the dome own 26% claim — two damping ratios for one medium (detail_evidence); (c) supremum theorem: H(r)=8537*exp(-r/8619) has sup H=8,537 km at r=0, so the 9,086 km and 9,572 km heights the V12 curve claims to reconcile both exceed the function maximum (detail_extra). Verdict Self-Contradicted holds.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard ionospheric physics (Sentman 1990, doi:10.1016/0021-9169(90)90113-2; Sentman 1995 in Volland Handbook) reproduces 7.83 Hz and all five harmonics from Maxwell equations with measured sigma(h) profiles. The dome renames the 10.59->7.83 Hz residual as aetheric damping without a new numerical prediction.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: The 7.83 Hz Schumann fundamental has been in the published observatory record since the 1950s-60s and was publicly indexed before the dome monitor commit; the monitor hardcodes the target on the same commit as the data-fetch line, so the temporal ordering the dome author own definition requires cannot be established from repo history.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The 10.59 Hz starting point is the globe formula (R=6,371 km), not dome geometry. Applying the dome own H(r) gives 22-35 Hz (spatial averages) or an 8.78 Hz floor — none equal to 7.83 Hz — so the confirming value is adopted, not derived from dome parameters.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is correct that measured Schumann resonance (7.83 Hz) sits ~26% below the idealized textbook 10.59 Hz value (data/wins.json:002 detail_evidence), and that a lossy cavity does shift its resonant frequency — a real feature of resonator physics the dome invokes when it says the medium damps the resonance.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Being right that a gap exists does not make the gap a dome prediction. The 10.59 Hz is the globe formula f=(c/2pi a)sqrt2 (data/wins.json:002 detail_evidence), and standard finite-conductivity ionospheric physics (Sentman 1990, doi:10.1016/0021-9169(90)90113-2) already accounts for the residual. Worse, the dome self-contradicts: applying its own H0=8,537 km to the quarter-wave formula gives an 8.78 Hz floor needing only ~11% damping, not 26%, and the supremum bound sup H(r)=8,537 km at r=0 (data/wins.json:002 detail_extra) mathematically forbids the 9,086 km and 9,572 km heights the model claims its H(r) curve reconciles — so the verdict is Self-Contradicted, not merely unproven.

No new hole. Verdict Self-Contradicted holds; recommended_action no_change.
